blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Account JSON field rename is an unmarked breaking change) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (DROP COLUMN legacy_email is irreversible with no down migration or backup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Every existing client of the public HTTP API that reads `user_name` from an Account response finds the key missing after deploy and gets null/undefined or a deserialization error, with no warning. Mark it **BREAKING** in the release note (proposal.md#Release note only says "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase.") with what clients must do, or keep the old key readable during a deprecation window (e.g. serialize both `user_name` and `userName`, or version the endpoint) before removing `user_name`.
findings.title: Account JSON field rename is an unmarked breaking change

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running this migration destroys every value still stored in `users.legacy_email` (rows from the 2023 import), and unlike `0004_accounts.sql` it ships no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql`, so a rollback cannot restore the column or its data. Add a down migration that re-adds `legacy_email TEXT`, and a backup step (e.g. copy `id, legacy_email` to an archive table or dump) before the drop — or state in the plan why the data is disposable and how to recover.
findings.title: DROP COLUMN legacy_email is irreversible with no down migration or backup
